brief.title: Tea at the Ninth Stall
brief.premise: A hedge-witch tea merchant follows a travelling fair that appears only in leap-season, trying to win back her family's lost stall before the fair folds its lanes and moves on.
constraints: Conflicts are settled by bargains, contests and trade, never violence.

world.name: The Thistledown Fair
world.description: A travelling fair that unfolds its lanes only in leap-season, where stall rights are held in favours, debts are settled in trade, and the fair itself seems to remember every promise made under its lanterns.

locations.name: Leap Lane
locations.description: The fair's main way, which appears in an ordinary field at leap-season and folds away at season's end.

locations.name: The Ninth Stall
locations.description: A shuttered stall at the lane's turn whose lease was forfeited on an unkept favour a generation ago.

locations.name: The Kettle Commons
locations.description: The cluster of tea tents where merchants trade gossip, samples and favours.

locations.name: The Wishing Barn
locations.description: The tallykeepers' barn where every promised favour is written on a wishing tag and hung until kept.

factions.name: The Stallholders' Round
factions.description: The merchants who hold the fair's leases and vote the stall rights.

factions.name: The Tallykeepers
factions.description: The clerks who record every favour on wishing tags and judge disputes of debt.

factions.name: The Carter Kin
factions.description: The families whose wains carry the fair between fields and keep the lanes' secrets.

rules.statement: The fair exists only in leap-season; at season's end the lanes fold back into ordinary fields.
Debts at the fair are paid in favours, and a favour once promised must be kept before the fair moves.
No contest at the fair may risk harm; disputes go to the Tallykeepers and are settled by bargain or contest.
The Ninth Stall's lease can be claimed only by the family that lost it, before the third bell of closing day.

history.name: The First Fair
history.description: The fair appeared uninvited in a fallow field, traded for a season, and left a lane where none had been.

history.name: The Forfeit of the Ninth
history.description: A tea merchant's family lost their stall when a promised favour went unkept past the third bell.

history.name: The Tally Accord
history.description: The tallykeepers were given authority over favour-debts after a season of duelling claims.

conflicts.name: The Ninth Claim
conflicts.description: The Carter Kin are quietly selling the Ninth Stall's lease, while the family that forfeited it still holds a claim.

conflicts.name: The Favour Shortage
conflicts.description: More favours are owed than can be kept before closing day, and the tallykeepers must rule which debts ride with the fair.

characters.name: Poppy Wren
characters.description: A hedge-witch tea merchant who brews her family's recipes from a handcart, carrying the deed-story of the Ninth Stall her grandmother lost.
characters.motivation: To win back the stall that is the last of her family's name at the fair.
characters.goal: Prove her family's claim to the Ninth Stall before the third bell of closing day.
characters.flaw: She apologises before she speaks, and hears refusal before it comes.
characters.internal_conflict: She wants the stall but fears the fair will find her unworthy of it.
characters.external_conflict: The Carter Kin's sale of the lease is lawful unless her claim is proven first.

abilities.name: Taste-truthing
abilities.description: Tastes sincerity in a shared cup of tea, a small hedge-witch gift.

characters.arc: Poppy stops apologising for her claim and lets the fair judge it honestly.

characters.name: Damson Grey
characters.description: A carter-kin factor who found the Ninth Stall's lease bundled in an old ledger and means to sell it before the lanes fold.
characters.motivation: To turn a forgotten lease into the factor's share his kin never gave him.
characters.goal: Complete the lease sale before the family's claim can be proved.
characters.flaw: He believes the rules serve whoever reads them closest.
characters.internal_conflict: He knows the claim is real and tells himself a sale is a kind of settling.
characters.external_conflict: Poppy's claim and the tallykeepers' tags stand between him and the sale.

abilities.name: Lease-craft
abilities.description: Finds the clause that lets him do what fairness forbids.

characters.arc: Damson reads one clause too many and finds the lease reads him back.

characters.name: Mabel Thorn
characters.description: The eldest tallykeeper, who keeps the wishing tags and remembers the taste of every tea that ever sealed a bargain.
characters.motivation: To see debts kept and the fair's memory honoured.
characters.goal: Rule on the Ninth Stall claim by the tags alone.
characters.flaw: She lets the rules do the kindness she could do herself.
characters.internal_conflict: She found the forfeited favour long ago and kept it quietly on record.
characters.external_conflict: The carters resent any tallykeeper reading old tags aloud.

abilities.name: Tally memory
abilities.description: Recalls every wishing tag she ever hung, and who promised what.

characters.arc: Mabel finally speaks the old tag aloud and lets the fair remember with her.

relationships.description: Mabel teaches Poppy how the fair's memory can carry her claim.
relationships.conflict: Mabel will not rule early; Poppy wants certainty now.

relationships.description: Poppy's claim contests Damson's lease sale.
relationships.conflict: Only one of them can hold the stall at closing day.

storyboard.title: Tea at the Ninth Stall
storyboard.logline: A tea merchant proves her family's claim to a shuttered stall before the travelling fair folds its lanes for another year.

scenes.title: The Lanes Unfold
scenes.summary: Poppy wheels her cart up Leap Lane as the fair unfolds, and finds the Ninth Stall shuttered under a For Sale tag.
scenes.goal: Learn why the stall is being sold.
scenes.conflict: Her family's claim must be proved before the sale completes.
scenes.outcome: Poppy registers a claim with the tallykeepers.

scenes.title: The Factor's Ledger
scenes.summary: At the Ninth Stall, Damson Grey shows the lease bundled in a carter ledger and gives her until closing day to contest it.
scenes.conflict: The sale is lawful unless her family's claim is proven.
scenes.outcome: Poppy learns the forfeiture was an unkept favour, not a lost deed.

scenes.title: The Wishing Tags
scenes.summary: In the Wishing Barn, Mabel Thorn traces the forfeited favour on its original tag: it was promised, and kept, a generation late.
scenes.conflict: The tags rule claims, and this tag has a complication Mabel alone remembers.
scenes.outcome: The tag shows the favour was kept by Poppy's grandmother, too late to save the lease but true.

scenes.title: The Brewer's Contest
scenes.summary: At the Kettle Commons, Poppy stakes her claim on the fair's oldest contest: the family brew, tasted by the stallholders' round.
scenes.goal: Prove the family craft the claim rests on.
scenes.conflict: A lost contest forfeits the claim's standing.
scenes.outcome: Her grandmother's recipe wins the round's vote and the right to be heard.

scenes.title: Before the Third Bell
scenes.summary: At the Ninth Stall as the third bell nears, Mabel reads the old tag aloud and rules the kept favour restores the family's claim.
scenes.goal: Win the ruling before the bell.
scenes.conflict: Damson's sale closes at the third bell, whichever comes first.
scenes.outcome: The claim is upheld; the lease is Poppy's and Damson's ledger is impounded.

scenes.title: Tea at the Ninth Stall
scenes.summary: On closing day, Poppy opens the Ninth Stall, pays Damson's owed share fairly, and the fair folds its lanes with her family's name on the lease.
scenes.conflict: Victory that leaves a debt unpaid is only half a claim.
scenes.outcome: The stall reopens; every favour on the tags is kept.

evidence_summary: The world, cast and storyboard satisfy the brief's gentle travelling-fair setting; deterministic validators are clean and there are no blocking defects.
